### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via getPublicConfig (symbol, a method of class AuthManager), localSignIn (literal, a string literal in PUBLIC_AUTH_CONFIG_NON_FLAG_KEYS))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 31eb2aeda251563fc3c8cd3e68b9b467f808d371` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ad2879d457c91bb51399eb2bb611909dc82e2140` — the merge of head `183eb2266c2f7029eb26d60557ce76500845f177` into base `31eb2aeda251563fc3c8cd3e68b9b467f808d371`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ad2879d457c91bb51399eb2bb611909dc82e2140 && git checkout ad2879d457c91bb51399eb2bb611909dc82e2140
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 31eb2aeda251563fc3c8cd3e68b9b467f808d371 183eb2266c2f7029eb26d60557ce76500845f177 && git checkout -B drift-repro 31eb2aeda251563fc3c8cd3e68b9b467f808d371 && git merge --no-ff 183eb2266c2f7029eb26d60557ce76500845f177

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 31eb2aeda251563fc3c8cd3e68b9b467f808d371
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 31eb2aeda251563fc3c8cd3e68b9b467f808d371` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `9cebce8674bce8d67ce08b8b1e9b81bc8a0277c6`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-11-16T00:09Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6903608822; no lane request (owed per check-owed-reviews). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread (domain:ui lane); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Face: `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths` (main's copy) decides no face on these 33 paths and hands the choice to the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line, so this is the declaration face. Every path of the diff outside the prose faces was read, plus the cited code on `main` (`AuthManager.getCanonicalOrigin`, `getPublicConfig`, `AuthProvider.getAuthConfig`). No prior record; ids are fresh.

### ① Derived judgments

**M1 (must-fix) — this head ships the page without the served field it reads, and says otherwise.** `features.publicBaseUrl` is served by nothing: not at this head, not on `main` at `121017b9` (no hit in `packages/spec/src/api` or `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src`). `MobileAppPage` therefore lands in `unpublished` on every deployment, configured or not, and the new entry after Profile leads every signed-in user to a destructive alert whose remedy (set `OS_AUTH_URL`, restart) changes nothing. Three texts in the diff state the contract as live: the changeset body ("the one the server publishes as `features.publicBaseUrl` on `GET /api/v1/auth/config`", which ships in four CHANGELOGs), the `AuthPublicConfig` jsdoc in `ui/packages/auth/src/types.ts`, and `Fixes #29314`, which would close a card whose Ask 2 (use the configured public origin) is unmet. The PR body says so itself and the PR is a draft with `Waits-on: #34119, #34099`; that is the right posture, and this record confirms it rather than waives it. State of the two: #34099 is merged; #34119 is still open and holds `packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`. The head builds and tests green without either, because every test stubs the field. Close by landing the server half in this PR as the seat ruled (schema key, `getPublicConfig` line, `PUBLIC_AUTH_CONFIG_NON_FLAG_KEYS`, regenerated reference, a plugin-auth test, and one test that reads the field over the real door). That head carries a published schema, so its review is owed on the schema face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; this record does not cover it.

**S1 (should-fix) — "the code holds only this server's address" is copy, not a judged or pinned property.** The card ruled the payload as `objectos://connect?server=` plus the URL-encoded public base URL, and nothing else. No code step enforces that limit and no test pins it. Make the payload a normalised address built from the parsed URL, and pin it. Detail is withheld from this record and is with the seat.

**S2 (should-fix) — the `unpublished` remedy is wrong for the one case that will reach it.** Once the server half lands, `getCanonicalOrigin()` always answers (configured value, or the loopback fallback, which correctly lands in `unreachable`). `unpublished` then fires only against a server that does not serve the key at all, where setting `OS_AUTH_URL` cannot help. `unpublishedBody` in all 11 packs prescribes exactly that. Either drop the branch's remedy in favour of "this server does not offer it yet", or say why a blank value is reachable.

What holds, checked adversarially:
- Payload and persistence: the page reads only `getAuthConfig()`; no session, token, cookie or user field enters the link, nothing is stored, the clipboard is written on the user's click only, and `window.location` is never read (pinned by the unpublished test). The value is rendered as text and as `qrcode`'s own SVG in an image; it is never an href or markup.
- Reach: `isPublicHostAddress` is the old `isPublicHttpsAddress` body minus the scheme test; `.internal` was already refused at the base, so the Connect Agent caller's behaviour is unchanged. Localhost, loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, CGNAT, unique-local IPv6, single-label, `.local` and `.internal` are refused and pinned (13 addresses in `mobileConnect.test.ts`, two through the page, one in Playwright); non-http and bare values are refused; an absent or blank value shows the refusal, never a link.
- Locales: all 11 `@object-ui/i18n` packs carry the same 13 `mobileApp` keys with identical placeholders and no English fallthrough; all 11 platform-objects bundles carry `nav_account_mobile_app`, translated. A test in the diff pins key and placeholder parity for every built-in locale.
- CLI pin: the account app authors 13 nav ids at this head and the fold contributes one, so 14 is the right count; `account.app.ts` is unchanged on `main` since the base. The both-halves assertions (200 on account, 403 on setup) are untouched.

**N1 (nit)** — a public host on plain `http:` is `ready` and pinned as a CONTROL. The card is silent on it; the seat should confirm it against objectstack-ai/mobile#156 rather than leave it as a test's decision.
**N2 (nit)** — surrounding whitespace in the published value is not normalised before it is used. The server trims today; S1's normalisation closes it.
**N3 (nit)** — the host test is a heuristic with a short refusal list; the card's named cases are covered. Any widening belongs to a card of its own, since the Connect Agent widget shares it.
**N4 (nit)** — the CLI pin's bare count shows that one id joined, not which or where. "After Profile" and the `componentRef` to registered-ref pairing are pinned by no test.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/auth` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` is correct for `Metadata-protocol: none` (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: `none` takes `patch`), and the list matches the packages the diff moves; `packages/cli` changes a test only and `ui/e2e` is no package. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is honest and identical in the PR body and the changeset: nav entry, component ref, i18n namespace and the declared type key are all named, and nothing that worked is refused. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no author-writable key or value is added. The changeset body's served-field sentence is false at this head (M1) and the level must be re-read when the server half adds `packages/spec` and `plugin-auth` to the diff.

CI at this head: 70 check-runs, all completed; none failed, none running (58 success, 12 skipped opt-in or conditional jobs). Green CI does not answer M1: no test reads the field from a server.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: the file-surface widening to `account.app.ts` and its bundles is seat-approved (claim amendment 2) and matches the diff. The forced test edit in `packages/cli` is justified and correct (count verified above). "No store links" matches the card's Ask 3 (only when configured; nothing configures them). Cloud: no Cloud-specific code, as Ask 4 expects.
- `open_questions`: none open; the route question was answered by the seat (route A, name `publicBaseUrl`).
- `security_findings: withheld` in the dev report: read; this record's S1 is the rule-layer statement, the rest is with the seat.
- SQL push-down: not applicable; the diff adds no query, id materialisation or join.
- Held paths: `auth-endpoints.zod.ts` and `auth-manager.ts` are not touched, as the claim amendment ordered.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7c7c5ba446dca6b4aa6a43349da72d856c8b24ee`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/public-base-url.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/public-base-url.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts, packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.test.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, content/docs/references/api/auth-endpoints.mdx, ui/packages/auth/src/types.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/mobile-app/mobileConnect.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/mobile-app/mobileConnect.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/mobile-app/MobileAppPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/connect/deploymentReach.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/account-mobile-app-nav.test.ts, .changeset/29314-mobile-app-connect-qr.md

Read at 2026-11-16T02:39Z. Delta review of this head against FAIL 6903711181 at 9cebce86; claim: comment 6905415687; lane request 6905407996 on mailbox #33873. Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread (domain:ui#1 lane); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Face: `record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths` (main's copy, which differs from the working tree's and prints the same record) reads the schema face off these 43 paths, so this record is at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` and carries ④. Read: the whole delta `9cebce86..7c7c5ba4`, every path of the diff outside the prose faces against the branch point `571cf908`, and the cited code at this head (`AuthManager.getCanonicalOrigin`, `getPublicConfig`, the base-URL writers in `auth-plugin.ts` and `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`). The previous record's ids are judged by id first; new ids are fresh.

### ① Derived judgments

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Prior findings, by id:
- **M1: closed.** `GET /api/v1/auth/config` serves `features.publicBaseUrl` at this head: `getPublicConfig` adds it, `AuthFeaturesConfigSchema` declares it, `PUBLIC_AUTH_CONFIG_NON_FLAG_KEYS` classifies it, and `public-base-url.test.ts` reads it over the real `registerAuthRoutes` door on a real `AuthManager`. The three texts that stated the contract as live (changeset body, `AuthPublicConfig` jsdoc, `Fixes #29314`) are now true. Both waited-on PRs are merged and the `Waits-on:` line is gone.
- **S1: closed.** The payload is `objectos://connect?server=` plus the encoded address rebuilt from the parsed URL (scheme, host with a non-default port, path; nothing else), and every refusal shows that same rebuilt address, never the raw value. Pinned by eight normalisation rows, a row that the link's only parameter is `server`, a refused-address row and page-level rows, with CONTROLs.
- **S2: closed.** `unpublishedBody` in all 11 packs names no setting (zero `OS_AUTH_URL` hits) and says the server does not offer the address yet; the page test pins it.
- **N1: closed.** A public host on plain `http:` is refused as `not-https` with its own title and body in all 11 packs, pinned with a CONTROL on `https:`. The lane reports this as the seat's ruling.
- **N2: closed.** The value is trimmed and normalised before use, with a row.
- **N3: stands, unchanged.** Still a heuristic shared with Connect Agent; a card of its own, not this PR.
- **N4: closed.** `account-mobile-app-nav.test.ts` pins the entry immediately after Profile, its `componentRef` and that it is ungated, with a CONTROL that the app parses; the page test resolves the same ref through the component registry. The CLI count comment now says which id joined.

New at this head:

**N1 (nit, new)** — with no base URL configured the door serves the auth layer's loopback fallback rather than omitting the key. The describe, the jsdoc and a CONTROL say so, and the page needs it to give the right remedy, so this is a stated design and not a defect; it is still a fallback served on a pre-login door, and the seat should confirm it rather than inherit it. Detail is with the seat.
**N2 (nit, new)** — the two door tests pin what the value contains, not that it comes from configuration alone. The code reads configuration only (checked below); one more row would pin it. Detail is with the seat.
**N3 (nit, continues prior N3)** — the host heuristic's short refusal list, unchanged.
**N4 (nit, new)** — a configured value that is not an absolute URL is served as nothing, and the page then tells the reader to update the server, which is the wrong remedy for a mis-set `OS_AUTH_URL`. Reachable only by operator error; the describe states the absence truthfully.

What holds, checked adversarially:
- Source of the served value: `publicBaseUrlOf(this.getCanonicalOrigin())`, and `getCanonicalOrigin` reads `config.baseUrl` only. Nothing of the request enters it, and no bind address or interface address does. The writers of `config.baseUrl` are the plugin option, `setRuntimeBaseUrl`, and the development port correction that only ever rewrites a loopback base.
- Shape of the served value: scheme, host and path. A credential, query or fragment in the setting is not served, and the test asserts that over the whole response body, not only the key.
- Merge commit `69238546`: `git merge-tree --write-tree b477713d 571cf908` yields tree `257161cc`, identical to the commit's tree. No hand edit.
- #34119 resolution: against the branch point, which already holds #34119, `auth-endpoints.zod.ts` differs by the seven added lines of the new key only; the `admin` describe and the regenerated `auth-endpoints.mdx` rows carry #34119's wording.

### ② Semver level

`Metadata-protocol: added` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, identical in the PR body and the changeset. The key is served, not authored, but it enters `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, and the level gate refuses `none` beside a moved baseline, so `added` is the declaration the rule requires. `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-auth` (the packages that carry the key) and on `@objectstack/platform-objects` (same fixed group, so the level is shared either way) satisfies AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3; `patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/auth` is right for packages that only read the key. The package list matches what the diff moves; `packages/cli` changes a test only and `ui/e2e` is no package. Nothing that worked is refused, so no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed. `Skills-docs: none` with its reason holds: no skill teaches the auth config payload.

Baselines: only `authorable-surface/api.json` records keys of this schema (one line added, in order). `api-surface`, `json-schema.manifest`, `declaration-map`, `export-origins` and `authorable-defaults` record the schema's name or its defaults, neither of which moves, and are correctly untouched. The reference page gains the row in both tables with the describe verbatim.

CI at this head is NOT green: 68 check-runs, 22 success, 11 skipped, 34 still running (all Test UI and Test Core shards, Build Core, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, the type checks and lints), and 1 failed: `Check Changeset`. Its log shows it judged a PR body that still read `Metadata-protocol: none`; the body and the changeset now both read `added`, so the failure is of the superseded body and not of this tree, but it stands on the head until the check is re-run. This PASS is of the contract only. The seat waits for the running checks and for a green `Check Changeset` before acting on it.

CI completed before posting: 72 check-runs, 58 success, 11 skipped, 3 failure. `Check Changeset` was re-run on the corrected body and is green; the red run is the superseded one. `Test UI (5/16)` and its roll-up are red on one case, `AppContent.disabledPackageDeepLink-13052.test.tsx` (the 404 CONTROL, at its timeout), a file this PR does not touch; the other 4698 UI tests pass, including this PR's. The lane re-runs that shard before queueing; this record does not stand in for it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: the file-surface widening (account app and bundles; `auth-endpoints.zod.ts` and `auth-manager.ts` after both waited-on PRs merged; the new `public-base-url.ts`) is reported as seat-approved and matches the diff. The three forced test edits are each the direct consequence of the added key or entry and are correct: the CLI count 14, the spec served-features fixture, the exact `features` expectation in `auth-manager.test.ts`.
- `open_questions`: none.
- `security_findings: withheld` in the dev report: read. This record's N1 and N2 are the rule-layer statements; the rest is with the seat.
- SQL push-down: not applicable; the diff adds no query, id materialisation or join.
- Draft: the PR is still a draft at this read.

### ④ Design judgment

- `packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`: `publicBaseUrl` is `z.string().optional()` with a describe, on `AuthFeaturesConfigSchema`, the seat's ruled route and name. The describe was checked clause by clause against the code and is true: the setting order is `os serve`'s, the sub-path is kept, `https://` is prepended to a bare host, the loopback fallback is served when none is set, the value is an address only, the console refuses a loopback or private address or a public host on plain `http:`, and the key is absent when the value is not an absolute URL. Optional is right: an older server omits it and the first consumer handles the absence. It holds against its first consumer, `MobileAppPage`, which reads exactly this key and nothing else.
- `packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts`: the key joins `PUBLIC_AUTH_CONFIG_NON_FLAG_KEYS` with a jsdoc naming its reader and that it gates no spec input, which is the register's own rule for a non-flag key; the spec test that requires the fixture to name every classified key is extended accordingly.
- `auth-manager.ts` and `public-base-url.ts` agree with the contract: one line builds the value, one spreads it only when present.
- `mobileConnect.ts` and `MobileAppPage.tsx` agree with the card's ruled payload and with the describe's refusal clause; the console repeats the normalisation rather than trusting the server, which is the right side to err on.

## 席位核对

Verdict: **ACCEPT** · head `183eb226` · 2026-11-16T04:55Z

1. **Shape.** `Fixes #29314`. 43 files: the console's Mobile App page in the account app, the `mobileApp` i18n namespace, and the server half (`features.publicBaseUrl` on `GET /api/v1/auth/config`), with one changeset.
